Issued at 209 AM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Early this morning, Water vapor satellite imagery along with upper 
air analysis showed an upper trough across the Great Basin. A broad 
upper level ridge axis extended across the southwest US, northeast 
into central high Plains. An upper level trough extended from the 
eastern Great Lakes, south-southwest across the east central CONUS.

The 6Z surface map showed a surface cold front extending from 
northeast ND, southwest into southwest SD, then southwest into 
northern WY. Light southeast winds were noted across much of the CWA 
with temperatures in the mid 60s to around 70 degrees.

Today through Tuesday:

The H5 trough across the Great Basin will shift east-southeast 
across the High Plains Today. The surface front across SD and 
northern WY will slowly push southeast into northern NE. The H5 ridge
axis will build east across KS and OK. Highs Today will reach to 
around 90 across much of the area, with lower to mid 90s across the 
western counties. Southerly wind will allow dewpoints to remain in 
the mid to upper 60s. Heat indices may be a couple degrees higher 
then the ambient temperature this afternoon. 

Monday night through Tuesday, a lead H5 trough will lift northeast 
from the SD/NE border into the upper Midwest but the broad upper 
trough will continue across the central Rockies and northern Plains. 
Due to convection across NE, an outflow boundary may push the front 
farther south late Monday night into Tuesday morning. The NAM 12 and 
GFS forecast isolated showers and thunderstorms developing ahead and 
behind the surface front across north central KS. However, the 
stronger ascent ahead of the H5 trough will be across NE and points 
northeast. Most numerical models show the front slowly pushing 
southward across western KS and across the northern and western 
counties of the CWA. The lead H5 trough will lift northeast across IA
on Tuesday, so there may not be much ascent for showers and 
thunderstorms ahead or north of the surface front.

Tuesday night through Thursday, a second H5 trough will dive 
southeast into the base of the broad H5 trough across the northern 
and central Plains. The southern edge of the H5 trough will dig 
southeast across much of KS. The DCVA ahead of the H5 trough will 
provide stronger ascent for scattered showers and thunderstorms along
and north of the frontal boundary late Tuesday night into Thursday 
morning. The H5 trough will dig southwest into the Mid MS River 
valley and the surface front will pass southeast of the CWA. The 
showers and storms will push southeast of the CWA during the late 
morning hours of Thursday. Skies may become partly cloudy Thursday
afternoon.

There may be a few strong to severe thunderstorms Wednesday 
afternoon along and southeast of the surface front. The front 
will push southeast across east central KS during the afternoon 
hours of Wednesday. The NAM12 and GFS forecast MLCAPE values of 
1200-2200 J/kg and effective shear of 25 to 35 KTS ahead of the 
front. The primary hazard would be damaging wind gusts and quarter
size hail if any storms did become severe.

Highs on Tuesday will be cooler northwest of the outflow 
boundary/front across the northwest counties, with highs in the 
lower 80s. Most of the area ahead of the front will see highs in the 
lower to mid 90s

Highs on Wednesday will be dependent on the location of the front. 
Behind the front across the northwest counties, high may only reach 
the mid to upper 70s, while southeast of the front across east 
central KS, highs will reach the lower 90s. 

Thursday the front will be southeast of much of the CWA. Highs will 
reach the lower to mid 80s, with mid to upper 80s across the 
southeast counties.

Thursday night through Friday night:  

The H5 ridge will retrograde 
westward across the southwest US. The mid level flow will be 
northwesterly. The front will become stationary across southern KS 
and northern OK. Any perturbations embedded in the northwesterly flow 
aloft combined with isentropic lift may provide enough ascent for 
isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms. The front 
will undergo frontolysis as it lift northward across the region 
Friday night. 

Saturday through  Monday:

The H5 ridge axis will build east across the Plains early next week. 
Look for a warming trend with upper 80s to lower 90s for high 
temperatures on Saturday. Sunday and Monday, afternoon highs will 
reach the lower to mid 90s. Heat indices will increase to around 100 
degrees along and south of I-70 next Sunday and Monday, with mid to 
upper 90 degree heat indices across the northern counties. If 
dewpoints are a few degrees higher across east central KS, during 
the afternoon hours of both Sunday and Monday,  then heat indicies 
may reach around 105 degrees.
